originality.rationale: The 2022 article already contains the 3×3 normal rotation-decay example (Example 5), so neither the existence of an eventually positive/non-positive generator nor its general spectral criterion is new. The new statement counts every connected component of positivity failure throughout a free damping/frequency family, gives exact transition equations and proves unbounded counts in the minimal dimension. The source example fixes one parameter ratio and does not contain this count; broad eventual-positivity and cone-invariance theorems require additional time-dependent computations to yield it. Retrieved related records concern rational numerical propagators or infinite-dimensional barriers, not the same exact matrix-exponential time topology. Priority remains qualified by unindexed and older specialized literature.

value.rationale: A natural question in eventual-positivity theory is how often positivity can fail before the eventual positive regime. The theorem produces a complete two-parameter answer with exact components, endpoint equations and unique critical damping ratios, and shows arbitrarily large finite temporal complexity already in dimension three, whereas dimensions one and two forbid any intermittent positivity. The exact count is a structural invariant of a canonical rotation-decay semigroup, not an arbitrary numerical slice; no general theorem over all semigroups is asserted.
